grh_bbbec7330c09b3f004bf.title: Cupids Boomerang
paragraphs: Dr. Christian agrees to help the painfully shy Dan tell Sarah that he has loved her for years. At a charity dance the bachelor-club members tease the doctor into promising that he will make the proposal for Dan. The plan backfires spectacularly: when Dr. Christian tries to explain that someone wants Sarah as his wife, she assumes he means himself and accepts before he can correct her. With the town already congratulating them, the doctor cannot bring himself to humiliate Sarah by admitting the mistake, while Dan is crushed. Dr. Christian and his friends then stage a fake fire at Sarahs house with a homemade smoke bomb. Believing the house is burning, Dan rushes inside, carries Sarah out and finally blurts out his real feelings. Sarah admits that she loves Dan too and breaks her mistaken engagement to Dr. Christian, who pretends to take the rejection bravely. Once safely unengaged, he swears off matchmaking when another woman immediately tries to arrange yet another romantic introduction for him.

grh_bb081ab627cc6db8bb57.title: Reunion
paragraphs: Fred Heming and Gwen unexpectedly meet again thirty-five years after a youthful romance ended when Gwen failed to reach the train that carried Fred away. As they compare memories, she finally explains that her car ran out of gas after her young brother secretly siphoned fuel, while Fred admits he had taken her absence as rejection and allowed their letters and lives to drift apart. Now widowed and divorced, they spend several days rediscovering the ease they once had together while also confronting the families and disappointments that shaped them in the intervening years. Fred asks Gwen to leave with him and gives her a second version of their old test: meet him at the airport if she wants a future together. Encouraged by her daughter to choose happiness, Gwen arrives in time, and the couple decides not to lose another chance.

paragraphs: Fontaine Harris, Vernon Crawley, Millie and their companions head for California with money left from their earlier adventures and discover that their invented connection to the motion-picture business can be turned into something real. grh_bb9935b5197769f5c7f4.title: Spotlight On Grandma
paragraphs: Grandma Benson has spent years raising her daughter's children and keeping the Forbes household running, but realizes that the family now notices her mainly when a blouse needs mending or some other chore is unfinished. Dr. Christian suggests that she finally take a vacation and let them discover how much they depend on her. Grandma goes considerably further: after hearing of a wealthy man's old sweetheart, Marie Monahan, she stages a supposed kidnapping and leaves a ransom note claiming she is the missing heiress and needs old love letters to prove it. Her frantic family suddenly listens to every story about her younger days and searches the house in panic. When Grandma returns safely, Dr. Christian reveals that he knew the heiress story could not be true. The kidnapping was Grandma's own theatrical way of turning the spotlight on a woman her family had taken for granted.
GRH catalogs [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]]'s "Spotlight On Grandma" for July 10, 1946, as episode 398.
